base_override.reason: SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH (title insurer consolidating annuity/life insurer F&G): the engine's OCF-based conservative OE is rejected as the base — for an insurer consolidating F&G, operating cash flow is policyholder plumbing, not distributable earnings: annuity deposits and the build in future policy benefits run through OCF while the corresponding investment deployment sits in investing (purchases of investment securities $23,198M in FY2025). FY2025 OCF was $5,828,000,000 against net income of $602,000,000, and NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE fires for 2023, 2024 and 2025; the engine's normalized OCF base is $23.6827/share — a 59.5% OE yield at $39.80 for a company whose filed diluted EPS was $2.21 in FY2025. Capitalizing that base prints a fake Tier S. For an insurer, net income is the honest owner's-earnings proxy (the ALLY/FUTU/LPLA/WSE/ARCC sector precedent in this sweep): SBC is already expensed inside it, title claim provisions and F&G benefit/reserve charges are already charged inside it, and the median-of-3-FY normalization mirrors the engine's own base method applied to that definition. The median is conservative for this name: FY2025 net income carries an abnormal tax load (income tax $753,000,000 on pre-tax $1,397,000,000, a 54% rate, including the F&G-distribution deferred-tax adjustment in Corporate & Other, which lost $458M attributable in FY2025), and GAAP NI is below adjusted net earnings in every recent year (H1 2026 adjusted EPS $2.31 vs GAAP $1.98). Declared under bounded authority (c): every input is a figure printed by this run's engine output (financials_history.csv).
base_override.source: Median of the last 3 fiscal years' net income per diluted share, built exclusively from this run's financials_history.csv (engine-filed figures): FY2023 net income $517,000,000 / 271,000,000 diluted shares = $1.9077; FY2024 $1,270,000,000 / 273,000,000 = $4.6520; FY2025 $602,000,000 / 272,000,000 = $2.2132; median of the three = $2.2132 (the FY2025 value; it is also the filed FY2025 diluted EPS attributable to common shareholders)

The value is not an estimate — it is the FY2025 figure printed in the FY2025 10-K Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows for the line that is this filer's capex, corroborated by the same statement's FY2024/FY2023 figures ($146M / $132M).
capex_override.reason: DATA_GAP:capex — capex missing for fiscal year(s) 2023, 2024, 2025 of the last 3 in EDGAR companyfacts under every candidate tag the engine reads (statements.json warning: no capital-expenditure figure filed for 45 periods with operating cash flow, 2015-06-30..2026-06-30), because FNF prints its capex only as the combined line 'Additions to property and equipment and capitalized software' in the 10-K cash-flow statement. The engine applies this single FY2025 filing value to every missing period; it overstates FY2024 capex by $1M (true $146M) and FY2023 by $15M (true $132M) — neither moves the verdict, the scored base is the NI-based base_override (net income already carries depreciation and amortization), and capex at ~$140M/yr is ~2.5% of the rejected OCF base either way.
capex_override.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-26), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows (pp. 107-108), investing activities line 'Additions to property and equipment and capitalized software': $(147) million for FY2025, with $(146) million for FY2024 and $(132) million for FY2023 in the same statement (all in $ millions); the statement reconciles exactly with this line (FY2025 operating $5,828M + investing -$8,934M + financing $2,263M = the reported net change in cash of -$843M; FY2024 and FY2023 reconcile the same way)

moat_justification: Moderate/narrow: the largest U.S. title insurer with scale, agency/direct distribution, title-plant data and industry-leading adjusted pre-tax title margins (15.9% FY2025, 17.8% in Q2 2026), plus F&G (AUM before flow reinsurance $73.1B at FY2025, $74.7B at Q2 2026) diversifying earnings away from housing — against a commodity, rate-filed product with no structural pricing power, earnings hostage to housing/mortgage volumes and F&G market/credit marks, and a return record that does not support a wide moat: fundamentals.json carries no roic_proxy or gross margin for an insurer presentation (both null), and GAAP ROE was 7.5% in FY2023, 16.4% in FY2024 and 8.1% in FY2025 (21.2% in FY2022, 29.7% in FY2021 in the title boom) — volatile and mostly below a wide-moat level through the recent cycle. A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years.
